card_summary: Miri will debut the V410 Live 4K Encoder/Decoder at the 2026 NAB Show. The product will be showcased in North America for the first time. The V410 supports ST 2110 and AES67, enabling low-latency transport of live 4K signals over IP networks. It also features 12G-SDI interfaces for traditional SDI connectivity, ensuring frame-accurate and genlock-capable signal transmission.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Miri V410 Live 4K Encoder/Decoder Reduces Latency with JPEG XS and ST 2110 Compliance

The Miri V410 Live 4K Encoder/Decoder is set to make its North American debut at the 2026 NAB Show, announced by the company as a solution for low-latency live 4K video transmission. This technology utilizes JPEG XS compression and is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110 standards, making it suitable for broadcast applications where signal integrity and real-time transport are crucial. The V410's support for 12G-SDI and IP connectivity also allows for flexible deployment in various broadcast environments.

Operational ROI

The Miri V410 Live 4K Encoder/Decoder offers significant operational savings for broadcast CTOs by reducing transmission costs associated with traditional satellite or fibre-based video transmission methods. With its ability to encode and decode 4K video in real-time using JPEG XS, the V410 can achieve latency as low as 1-2 ms, which is significantly lower than traditional methods. This reduction in latency directly affects the live production workflow, enabling more efficient signal routing and reduced hardware rack footprint, as fewer devices are required to manage signal delay compensation.

In comparison to existing approaches, the V410's compliance with ST 2110 and use of JPEG XS compression simplifies the signal routing process by allowing for IP-based transmission, which can be more easily managed and switched than traditional SDI signals. This operational change can lead to reduced labour costs and increased flexibility in live production environments, as engineers can more easily manage and monitor signal flows. Additionally, the reduced latency and improved signal integrity provided by the V410 can also lead to improved viewer experience, as live events can be transmitted with minimal delay and without signal degradation.

Security & Integration

The Miri V410 Live 4K Encoder/Decoder is designed to integrate seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, with support for SMPTE ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67 standards. This ensures compliance with relevant cybersecurity requirements and allows for secure transmission of live video signals over IP networks. The V410's use of JPEG XS compression also provides a secure and efficient method for transmitting high-quality video signals, with built-in support for encryption and authentication. Additionally, the device's support for RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) protocol ensures reliable and secure transmission of video signals over the internet, making it suitable for remote production and contribution applications.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The Miri V410 requires a minimum of 10GbE network connectivity to support 4K video transmission, and is compatible with a range of hardware and software platforms, including those supporting NMOS IS-04 and S3-compatible APIs.
  • Compatibility: The V410 is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and supports JPEG XS compression, ensuring seamless integration with existing ST 2110-based systems and devices.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming updates to the ST 2110 standard, which are expected to include new specifications for IP-based audio and video transmission, and how these updates may impact the deployment and operation of devices like the Miri V410.

The introduction of the Miri V410 Live 4K Encoder/Decoder to the North American market signals a significant shift towards IP-based live video transmission, with a focus on low-latency and high-quality signal integrity. As such, engineering teams should begin evaluating the V410 and similar devices for potential deployment in their live production environments, with a focus on integrating these devices into existing ST 2110-based systems and workflows.

Analysis: Miri V410 supports ST 2110, enabling low-latency 4K video transport over IP networks with bitrates up to 50 Gbps, simplifying live event streaming workflows.
